    # Mechanism inferred from evidence:
    # 1. Leading whitespace is preserved exactly [E4, E6, E7, E8, E10].
    # 2. Trailing whitespace is stripped [E3, E4, E5, E7, E9, E10].
    # 3. The first character of the remaining string is uppercased [E1..E12].
    #    - If it's a letter, uppercase it (é->É, ü->Ü, ß->SS) [E6, E8].
    #    - If it's a digit or punctuation, leave it [E2 "1ABC"->"1abc", E8 "!abc"->"!abc"].
    # 4. All other characters are lowercased [E1..E12].
    #    - Unicode lowercasing applies (ÉLAN->élan before first-char upper) [E6, E8].
    # 5. Tabs/newlines are whitespace: leading preserved, trailing stripped [E10].
    #    - Note E10 "a\tb" -> "A\tb": first char 'a' uppercased, rest lowercased.
    #    - "hello\t" -> "Hello": trailing tab stripped.
    # 6. Empty / all-whitespace strings: leading whitespace preserved, but the
    #    whole string of only spaces becomes "" [E4 "   "->""].
    #    Actually "   " -> "": all whitespace is trailing after no content.
    #    But "  hello" keeps leading spaces. So: strip trailing whitespace,
    #    then if nothing left, result is "".
    # 7. The first-char uppercase only applies to the first non-whitespace?
    #    Check: "  hello world" -> "  hello world" (unchanged, lowercase h) [E6].
    #    " hello" -> " hello" [E2]. " Example" -> " example" [E7].
    #    So if there is leading whitespace, NO first-char capitalization happens.
    #    The whole string is just lowercased (after trailing strip).
    #    Confirm: "  Hello World" -> "  hello world" [E6]. Yes.
    # 8. So the rule: strip trailing whitespace. If leading whitespace present,
    #    lowercase everything. Otherwise, uppercase first char, lowercase rest.
    #    " Zebralower" -> " zebralower" [E1]. Yes.
    #    "  mixed CASE  " -> "  mixed case" [E4,E8]. Yes.
    #    " one two" -> " one two" [E4]. Yes.
    #    "hello world 123" -> "Hello world 123" [E12]. Yes.

    def transform(s):
        # Strip trailing whitespace only
        s = s.rstrip()
        if not s:
            return ""
        # If starts with whitespace, just lowercase everything
        if s[0].isspace():
            return s.lower()
        # Otherwise uppercase first char, lowercase the rest
        first = s[0]
        rest = s[1:]
        # Uppercase first char (may expand, e.g. ß -> SS)
        upper_first = first.upper()
        return upper_first + rest.lower()

    return {"outputs": [transform(x) for x in probe["inputs"]]}
